neighbours.label: preposition after a verb of falling or being sent away (fell from, blown into, given up for)
fire: During the storm a heavy branch broke off and fell from the old oak.
The vase slipped out of her hands and dropped onto the stone floor.
Hailstones as big as marbles came tumbling from the dark clouds.
In the end the baby was given up for adoption by her young mother.
The explosion hurled pieces of the hull into the sea.
He lost his grip and slid off the wet roof into the bushes.
The leaves were swept away by the wind before we could rake them.
A loose stone rolled down from the cliff and blocked the path.
quiet: During the storm a heavy branch made the old oak creak loudly.
The vase she bought at the market sits on the stone floor.
Hailstones as big as marbles were reported in the evening news.
In the end the baby was named after her young mother.
The explosion was heard by sailors on the other side of the harbour.
He kept his footing and finished painting the wet roof.
The leaves turned red and gold before we could rake them.
A loose stone in the wall was repaired by the farmer.
